messages:
ana (support): Hey team, customer 'AcmeChat' opened an escalation — ~20% of requests to hosted rw-large are returning 504/gateway_timeout since 09:10 UTC. They see a spike on peak and say retries don't help. billing unaffected. Can we triage?

markus (eng-sre): Thanks Ana. Any request ids or sample traces? 504s usually mean gateway -> upstreams timed out (scale-up lag).

ana (support): oops typo, Ana. Sent logs in DMs. Sample request_id: r-0a12b3c4. Trace shows gateway waiting ~60s then 504.

lina (runtime): Pulling metrics now. KEDA scaler for rw-large shows metric (queueLength) ramped from 5 -> 220 in 30s. HPA target CPU jump didn't trigger fast enough. Looks like minReplicas is 0 for that pool.

ops-oncall: Confirming: minReplicas: 0, cooldown period 90s, pollingInterval 30s, scaleDownStabilization 300s. KEDA ScaledObject has cooldown 60s. There may be a mismatch.

markus (eng-sre): Can you paste the ScaledObject and HPA snippet? Also any pod startup logs (model load) — if startup is >30s then scale-up won't fix 50 concurrent reqs fast enough.

lina (runtime): Dumping snippets:
```yaml
# ScaledObject (trimmed)
minReplicaCount: 0
maxReplicaCount: 20
pollingInterval: 30
cooldownPeriod: 60
triggers:
  - type: azure-queue
    metadata:
      queueLength: "20"
```
```yaml
# HPA (trimmed)
minReplicas: 0
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60
```

lina (runtime): Pod startup logs show model load ~24s on gpu nodes but when cold fetch from object-store it spikes to ~85s when many pods boot at once. Cache misses.

ana (support): Customer says failures align with scheduled marketing bursts at 09:10. They don't keep min capacity during bursts.

markus (eng-sre): Root cause probable: zero-min + cooldown + object-store cold load => scale-up lag -> gateway waits -> 504s. Also KEDA threshold too high (queueLength:20) — too late.

ops-oncall: Quick mitigation options: 1) bump minReplicas to 2 for this pool, 2) lower KEDA pollingInterval to 15s and reduce threshold to 5, 3) pre-warm hook to populate cache during known bursts.

lina (runtime): Agreed. Another mitigation: reduce readinessProbe initialDelay and use warmup probe that returns ready after KV cache primed. We can also serve from a warm pool (warm replicas with model in memory but marked low traffic).

markus (eng-sre): Repro steps for oncall to validate before rolling to customer:
1) simulate burst with loadtest script (k6) hitting /v1/generate 200rps for 1m against a test cluster.
2) set minReplicas=0, deploy ScaledObject as above and run loadtest -> expect >50% 504 within 30-90s.
3) apply mitigation (minReplicas=2, pollingInterval=15, queueLength=5), rerun -> expect >95% success after initial ramp.

ops-oncall: I'll run step 1-3 in staging now. Sharing commands:
```bash
kubectl -n hosted get scaledobject rw-large -o yaml > /tmp/so.yaml
# edit /tmp/so.yaml -> set minReplicaCount: 2 pollingInterval: 15 triggers[0].metadata.queueLength: "5"
kubectl apply -f /tmp/so.yaml
# run k6 from worker box
k6 run --vus 100 --duration 60s scripts/rw_burst.js --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086
```

sre-bot: paging ops-oncall (oncall schedule matched). Incident annotated: incident/1792345678 - autoscale-scaleup-lag

ops-oncall: running now. initial warmup shows model load ~25s; cold start 80s. with minReplicas=2 new requests average latency 300ms after model in memory.

markus (eng-sre): Good. For prod we should:
- Policy: set minReplicas >= 2 for high-traffic models or during scheduled events
- KEDA: reduce threshold/polling during business hours, or use external scaler that looks at request rate not queue length
- Runtime: introduce a 'fast-path' where gateway can route to fallback smaller quantized variant to avoid 504s when rw-large cold.

lina (runtime): I'll open a runtime PR for warm-pool and a readiness/warmup probe. Rough ETA: 3 working days for prototype.

tim (customer-success): I'll propose immediate workaround to customer: enable pre-warm schedule during marketing windows and bump min replicas. They asked for rollout guidance.

ana (support): Customer ok with temporary minReplicas=2. They want us to monitor for 48h and then reconvene.

markus (eng-sre): Action items:
- ops-oncall: apply temp config to production for AcmeChat (minReplicas=2, pollingInterval=15) — in next 10m (assigned)
- lina: PR for warm-pool/readiness probe (ETA 3d)
- tim: notify customer + collect telemetry for 48h
- markus: follow up on KEDA scaler tuning options and fallback routing (ETA 2d)

ops-oncall: temp config applied to prod for that pool at 09:45 UTC. Monitoring alert rule created for 504 rate > 1% (5m).

ana (support): Noted, customer notified and appreciated the quick patch.

markus (eng-sre): Leaving this thread open until 48h monitoring completes. If 504s reappear we'll escalate to product for fallback variant rollout.

lina (runtime): Adding internal note: object-store parallelism causing cold load spike. We'll add cached warm copies on local SSD via background prefetcher in runtime PR.

ops-oncall: Staging results attached (link): https://internal.metrics/acme/1792345678 — pre/post charts show 504s drop from 22% -> 0.4% after minReplicas change.

ana (support): closing interim: monitoring ongoing, customer happy with temp fix. Will reopen if any regression. :thumbsup:
